s.t:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
To support this ambitious goal, we are seeking an Electrical Test Technician to join our Electrical Integration & Test Team in Munich. You will be responsible for the assembly, integration, maintenance, and modification of electrical test systems used throughout the development, verification, and validation of spacecraft subsystems and avionics equipment.
You will play a key role in building and maintaining custom test racks, integrating commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and custom-designed hardware, and supporting engineers during test campaigns. Working closely with electrical, avionics, and system engineers, you will help ensure our test infrastructure meets the highest standards of quality, reliability, and safety.

s.h: In your role as Electrical Test Technician, you will
s.t:
Assemble, wire, and integrate electrical test racks and ground support equipment
Perform wiring and interconnections between COTS equipment and custom-designed hardware
Manufacture, route, label, and install electrical harnesses and cables according to engineering documentation
Interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings to perform integration and troubleshooting activities
Support electrical integration, verification, and test campaigns across multiple projects
Perform inspections, modifications, and repairs on electrical assemblies and test equipment
Assist in the installation, replacement, and rework of electronic components on PCBs when required
Execute continuity, insulation, and basic electrical verification tests on assemblies and harnesses
Maintain accurate documentation of wiring modifications, test setups, and configuration changes
Support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations on electrical and test systems

s.h: You and your team will be in charge of
s.t:
Building and maintaining reliable electrical test infrastructures for spacecraft development and qualification activities
Integrating a wide variety of electrical equipment, including power supplies, measurement devices, automation components, and custom electronics
Ensuring all rack assemblies and wiring installations comply with internal standards and safety requirements
Supporting engineers during test setup preparation, execution, and troubleshooting activities
Contributing to the continuous improvement of test equipment, assembly processes, and documentation practices
Maintaining high levels of workmanship, quality, and configuration control across all electrical integration activities
Ensuring electrical installations are safe, maintainable, and suitable for demanding aerospace test environments

Technical diploma, vocational qualification, or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, Industrial Automation, or a related field
Proven hands-on experience in electrical assembly, wiring, and integration activities
Ability to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation
Experience assembling and wiring electrical cabinets, racks, or industrial control systems
Knowledge of cable and wire selection principles, including preliminary conductor sizing based on electrical loads and installation constraints
Familiarity with common industrial automation components such as relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, sensors, power supplies, and I/O modules
Experience using standard electrical test equipment, including multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and continuity testers
Strong troubleshooting skills and a structured, methodical approach to problem-solving
High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship
Fluent in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced environment
Nice-to-Have Skills
Experience with aerospace, automotive, railway, or other highly regulated industries
Experience performing PCB assembly, component replacement, soldering, and electronic rework
Familiarity with low-voltage DC power distribution systems
Knowledge of cable harness manufacturing and connector assembly standards
Experience working with custom-built test equipment and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) environments
Ability to design rack front panels and front-end layouts for custom test systems
Familiarity with CAD tools for electrical or mechanical design documentation
Understanding of configuration management and documentation control processes

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:
We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind
We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them
We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

You will check the progress of jobs and resolve delays when possible.
You will train electricians and military technicians in all aspects of the electrical trade.
Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.

This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job. Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: Ability to Lead or Supervise.

Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification Handbook for Trades and Labor Occupations.

Who We Are
We're on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.

Help launch Sunrun's brand-new St. Louis branch! As America's #1 home solar and battery company, we are seeking an experienced Non-Certified Electrician to join our team starting now!
As a key member of our launch team, you will spend your first few months gaining hands-on leadership experience alongside our established Chicago team before permanently running installation crews out of our new St. Louis branch when doors open in early 2027.
Through our Power+ program, we invest heavily in your skills and career development, offering cross-training across solar, battery, and service operations to build long-term job security.

While supporting operations in Chicago during the pre-launch phase, Sunrun covers 100% of your travel overhead:
Rotation Schedule: 2 weeks on-site in Chicago, followed by 4 full days off at home in St. Louis.
Company Vehicle: Dedicated company vehicle provided for travel and work use.
Paid Travel Time: Full hourly compensation for time spent traveling between St. Louis and Chicago.
Lodging & Meal Allowance: 100% company-paid hotel accommodations plus daily per diem.

Electrical Installation & Interconnection: Lead or assist in the installation of electrical systems interconnecting residential solar arrays and battery storage systems to the power grid.
Service & Troubleshooting: Perform Main Panel Upgrades (MPUs), troubleshoot system issues, resolve electrical problems, and assist with necessary repairs or commissioning.
Crew Support & Leadership: Support the PV installation crew on-site and step up to lead the crew when the Foreperson is absent.
Code & Safety Compliance: Ensure work meets high workmanship standards, complies with current NEC and local codes, and strictly adheres to OSHA safety standards and Sunrun practices.
Inspections & Communication: Coordinate with local inspectors as assigned, and work closely with homeowners and branch teams to deliver a top-tier customer experience.

Education & Apprenticeship Hours: High school diploma or equivalent. Must possess 75% of the hours required to sit for state-specific electrical certification exams (Certified Electrical Trainee preferred or required depending on state regulations).
Electrical Experience: Hands-on electrical installation and repair experience, including work with wiring up to 600 VDC / 480 VAC. Working knowledge of replacing residential electrical services and distribution panels preferred.
Technical & Code Proficiency: Working knowledge of NEC codes, ability to interpret single-line drawings/PV system schematics from roof to meter, and solid understanding of solar interconnection principles and basic construction.
Driver Requirements: Must be at least 21 years old with a valid driver's license and a clean driving record (ability to pass a driving background check).
Soft Skills & Ownership: Strong troubleshooting and logical decision-making skills, customer focus, and a results-driven attitude with the ability to lead when necessary.
Physical Demands
Lifting & Transport: Ability to regularly transport materials and equipment up to 50 lbs (and up to 100 lbs with assistance).
Heights & Confined Spaces: Comfortable working on rooftops at various pitch angles, walking on rafters/shingles without causing damage, and maneuvering in attics, basements, or crawl spaces.
PPE & Safety Gear: Ability to work safely while wearing heavy protective equipment, including arc flash suits, gloves, face shields, and fall protection harnesses.
Environmental Exposure: Ability to work outdoors in varied weather conditions (extreme heat/cold, humidity, wet environments), low-light or full-sun settings, and around standard chemical materials.
Vision & Physical Function: Fine motor skills (manipulation, grasping, pinching), normal color vision (ability to distinguish wiring colors such as red, black, yellow, white, green), and clear hearing for safety commands.

· Intitulé du poste : Électricien AC/DC et technicien photovoltaïque

· Taux d'activité : 100 %

· Rattachement : Chef de projet / responsable technique

· Base : Siège GTS ; chantiers en Suisse romande

· Titre exigé : CFC d'installateur\-électricien — copie à joindre à la candidature

· Permis : Catégorie B exigé

· Entrée en fonction : À convenir

Réaliser la partie électrique des installations photovoltaïques GTS — AC et DC — et conduire seul les chantiers AC : matériel, planning, exécution, mesures, rapports. Mettre en service, mesurer, documenter, et rendre une installation fonctionnelle et conforme.

· Tirer, raccorder, mesurer, mettre en service et documenter.

· Prendre un chantier AC et le mener de bout en bout sans supervision continue.

· Être la référence technique sur le terrain quand une installation dysfonctionne.

· De la pose de modules à la journée : la partie mécanique est faite par les équipes de montage.

· Un poste de bureau : le terrain reste le cœur du métier.

· Un poste sans progression.
· Du résidentiel au bâtiment industriel. Objets courants de 10 à 500 kWc, avec des projets de plus grosse puissance en croissance.

C'est le cœur du poste. Il faut savoir le faire seul, dès l'entrée.
Installation et raccordement

· Pose et raccordement des tableaux : coffrets AC, TGBT, protections, DDR, parafoudres, sectionnements, appareils de mesure.

· Tirage et raccordement des câbles de puissance, dimensionnement contrôlé sur site, chemins de câbles, passages coupe\-feu.

· Mise à terre et liaisons équipotentielles : réalisation et vérification.

· Raccordement au point d'injection, coordination avec le GRD, pose et paramétrage des compteurs et du comptage de production.

· Reprise et modification d'installations existantes : identification des circuits, coupures planifiées, remise en service.
Conduite autonome d'un chantier AC
Un chantier AC confié doit revenir fini, mesuré et documenté.

· Lire le dossier technique, relever ce qui manque et clarifier avant de démarrer.

· Établir la liste de matériel complète et la transmettre à temps pour la commande.

· Planifier son propre travail : ordre des étapes, durées, coordination avec les autres corps de métier et avec le chef de projet.

· Organiser les moyens nécessaires : accès, échafaudage, nacelle, coupures, autorisations d'accès.

· Encadrer ponctuellement un apprenti ou un monteur sur la partie AC.

· Tenir le rapport journalier, les heures et les photos d'avancement.

· Signaler immédiatement tout écart de délai, de coût ou de faisabilité — le plus tôt possible.
Mesures, sécurité et documents
Sans documents, le chantier n'est pas fini.

· Contrôle propre de l'installation selon la NIBT et l'OIBT.

· Protocoles de mesure complets : continuité du conducteur de protection, résistance d'isolement, impédance de boucle, courant de court\-circuit, contrôle des DDR, ordre des phases, mesure de terre.

· Établissement du rapport de sécurité et des annexes, dans les délais et sans reprise.

· Respect des règles de sécurité au travail : cinq règles de sécurité, consignation, EPI, travail sous tension interdit sauf procédure.

· Signalement des non\-conformités constatées sur les installations existantes rencontrées.

s.h: 3\. PARTIE DC, MISE EN SERVICE ET MONITORING — SOUHAITÉE
s.t:
Souhaitée à l'entrée, indispensable à terme. Si elle n'est pas acquise, elle se forme chez nous — voir chapitre 6\.
Côté DC

· Câblage des strings, connectique, coffrets DC, sectionneurs, parafoudres, cheminements et fixations.

· Contrôle des strings avant mise sous tension : polarité, tension à vide, résistance d'isolement, courant de court\-circuit.

· Mesure de courbe I\-V et interprétation ; recherche de défaut de string, de défaut d'isolement et d'arc.

· Thermographie de contrôle et lecture des résultats.
Mise en service des onduleurs

· Mise en service et paramétrage des onduleurs string et centraux : réglages réseau, courbes de puissance, limitation d'injection, protection de découplage.

· Paramétrage conforme aux exigences du GRD et aux prescriptions de raccordement en vigueur.

· Rédaction du protocole de mise en service et du relevé des paramètres appliqués.

· Diagnostic et traitement des défauts d'onduleur, échange sous garantie, relation avec le support fabricant.
Monitoring et informatique

· Installation et configuration du monitoring : passerelles, compteurs, capteurs, bus de communication (Modbus RTU/TCP, RS485\), sondes d'irradiation et de température.

· Mise en réseau : adressage IP, VLAN, routeur 4G, VPN, ports, pare\-feu côté client — savoir dialoguer avec un service informatique.

· Contrôle de la remontée des données, alarmes et seuils, création des accès client.

· Analyse d'un écart de production : distinguer un défaut d'installation, un défaut de matériel, un ombrage et une erreur de paramétrage.

s.h: 4\. GROSSE PUISSANCE, BORNES ET BATTERIES — ATOUTS
s.t:
Non exigés à l'entrée, mais ce sont les domaines en croissance chez GTS. Une expérience dans l'un d'eux est un vrai plus.
Installations \> 500 kVA

· Tableaux de puissance, jeux de barres, câbles de forte section, raccordements sur transformateur.

· Sélectivité, coordination des protections, protection de découplage, contrôle de la qualité de réseau.

· Coordination avec le GRD sur les conditions de raccordement et les essais de conformité.
Bornes de recharge

· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de bornes AC et DC.

· Gestion dynamique de charge, délestage, comptage, communication et supervision (OCPP).

· Coordination avec la puissance disponible du bâtiment et l'autoconsommation PV.
Stockage batterie

· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de systèmes de stockage.

· Paramétrage des modes de fonctionnement : autoconsommation, écrêtage, alimentation de secours.

· Exigences de sécurité et de protection incendie applicables aux locaux de batteries.
Large autonomie sur le terrain, cadre clair sur ce qui engage l'entreprise.

· L'organisation de son chantier AC et l'ordre des étapes.

· Les choix de mise en œuvre, dans le respect des plans, de la NIBT et des règles de l'art.

· La liste de matériel et les besoins en moyens de chantier, transmis pour commande.

· L'arrêt d'une opération si les conditions de sécurité ne sont pas réunies — sans discussion ni justification ultérieure.

s.h: Propose, le chef de projet décide
s.t:
· Toute modification du périmètre, du matériel prévu ou de la solution technique.

· Tout travail supplémentaire demandé par le client sur le chantier.

In order to qualify, you must meet the general experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards Handbook X-118C. QUALIFICATIONS: Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Qualification Standard Handbook X-118C for the WG-2800 - Electrical Installation And Maintenance Family. .

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most blue-collar positions, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. The screen out element for this position is the ability To Lead without more than normal supervision.

JOB ELEMENTS: Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1.

Working knowledge of a wide range of principles, processes. and techniques of trade. technical practices in order to interpret drawings, plan, layout, install, modify, troubleshoot, and repair a variety of electrical systems, and of regulations, procedures, and policies related to maintenance and documentation. 2.

Knowledge of safety regulations, practlces, and procedures, 3. Knowledge of the use and maintenance of tools, equipment, and equipment common to trades and labor work performed by the group being led. 4.

Demonstrates exceptional hands-on skill and technical proficiency in performing and directing the specialized trade work of the electrical maintenance unit.

Proven ability to execute, oversee, and troubleshoot complex operations involving Lightning Protection Systems, high, medium, and low-voltage distribution systems, as well as industrial motors and control systems. 5. Ability to plan and organize work assignments to include determining resources required to accomplish mission.

Physical Effort:: The work requires regular and moderate-to-heavy physical exertion, The employee frequently performs moderately heavy lifting. pulling, and carrying Of equipment and materials weighing up to 18 kilograms (40 pounds) independently.

Occasionally, the incumbent is required to lift or pull heavy cables and equipment weighing in excess of 23 kilograms (50pounds) utilizing weight-handling equipment or with the assistance of other workers. The duties demand prolonged standing, as well as frequent bending, stooping, and climbing.

At times, the employee must perform tasks in awkward positions and restricted or confined spaces where precise physical coordination, balance, and manual dexterity of the hands, legs, and body are required.

Working Conditions: The incumbent works in both indoor and outdoor environments, With frequent exposure to high temperatures, intense noise, and vibrations in mechanical and electrical rooms, as well as extreme weather conditions when operating outdoors.

Working conditions within mechanical and electrical spaces frequently involve wet or slippery surfaces, poor illumination, unpleasant odors, gases, fumes, and contact with oils, lubricants, and chemical cleaning agents.

The nature of the work presents inherent operational hazards, subjecting the employee to potential electrical shocks, burns, chemical irritation, bruises, and strains. Duties regularly involve working from bucket trucks, climbing ladders, and operating on or around high-speed rotating machinery and energized electrical equipment.

TO mitigate these risks. the employee is required to strictly adhere to safety protocols and utilize specialized personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety shoes, protective eyewear, arc flash gear, insulated gloves, hearing protection, and any other equipment deemed necessary for specific environmental conditions.

PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.
